From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller SPA Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## How I treated the Seller's categorisation

The Seller's "Reviewer Efficiency Note" says that [STANDARD] clauses have been "reviewed and cleared by both sides". It also says the disclosure framework and limitation package are already "accepted". Nothing in the package supports either claim. They are the counterparty's assertions, so I have reviewed every item in full. Unless your deal team has actually agreed any of these points, please tell Seller's counsel that nothing is agreed until the Buyer's mark-up is returned.

Several Seller positions are contradicted by the Seller's own Disclosure Letter:

- **Bluefen:** "addressed" versus "consent NOT included".
- **Riverlark:** facility "NOT repaid".
- **Privacy incident:** "not material" versus "preliminary, scope unknown".
- **Bonuses:** "NOT in funds flow".

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap (cl 12.1)
- **Seller:** Aggregate cap of 20% of price (AUD 4.8m).
- **Buyer should want:** A general warranty cap of at least 40–50% of price (AUD 9.6m–12m). Fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities and fraud should sit outside this cap.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 50%, with a fallback of 30–35% only if W&I insurance is obtained at Seller cost.** Identified exposures (Bluefen ~30% of revenue, privacy incident, Ironquay IP) could exceed AUD 4.8m on their own.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket (cl 12.2)
- **Seller:** AUD 25k de minimis. AUD 250k basket (~1.04% of price), with only the excess recoverable.
- **Buyer should want:** A de minimis of AUD 10k. A basket of about 0.5% (AUD 120k) that is a tipping basket, so recovery is from the first dollar once exceeded. Related claims should aggregate for de minimis purposes. Specific indemnities, tax and fundamental claims should be excluded from both thresholds.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter.** A deductible basket combined with a 20% cap removes a large share of realistic recovery, and series claims (e.g. Sandbar) could otherwise be split under the thresholds.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit (cl 12.3 / 13)
- **Seller:** 18 months for general claims. Any limitation applies to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise".
- **Buyer should want:** 24 months for general warranties, which covers two full audit cycles post-Completion. Separate, longer periods should apply to tax, fundamental and indemnity claims.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter at 24 months, and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** That default silently imports 18 months into tax, title and indemnity claims.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental / Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties carry the same cap and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer should want:** A cap of 100% of the price. A time limit of at least 6 years, matching the contract limitation period under the *Limitation Act 1969* (NSW). No de minimis or basket, and no disclosure against them.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject outright.** If title fails, the Buyer has bought nothing, and recovery limited to 20% for that is not commercially tenable.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature". There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer should want:** An express carve-out disapplying all limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance and the knowledge qualifier for fraud, dishonesty or wilful concealment by the Seller, the Company or their representatives. Non-reliance should be confirmed not to exclude warranties and indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject, and insert a full fraud carve-out.** This is non-negotiable market practice, and the current drafting arguably attempts to limit fraud liability.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope (Schedule 7 / DL 1.1–1.2)
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (including DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records.
- **Buyer should want:** Only specific disclosures in the Disclosure Letter. Each must be fair, with sufficient detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter, and must be referenced to the warranty it qualifies. There should be no general data room or public-records disclosure. Disclosures must not qualify fundamental warranties, tax or specific indemnities. DL 1.4 (no admission) is acceptable only if it is not used to dilute a fair disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject general disclosure; accept specific, fair disclosure only.** Otherwise the warranties are effectively hollowed out by the whole data room.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, or that was discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer should want:** Deletion, with an express statement that the Buyer's knowledge or investigation does not prejudice any claim. As a fallback, limit it to the actual knowledge of named deal-team individuals of matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter. "Discoverable" and adviser knowledge must not count.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insert pro-sandbagging wording.** Combined with general disclosure, this would bar claims for the very risks the Buyer's due diligence has identified.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3; DD-002)
- **Seller:** "Addressed". Reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. DL item 2 confirms no final consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Buyer should want:** A condition precedent satisfied only by unconditional written consent in a form approved by the Buyer. If consent is conditional, any 11.3 conditions must be satisfied or acceptable to the Buyer, with no adverse change to terms or pricing. The Seller should use best endeavours. Only the Buyer may waive the condition, and the Buyer should have a termination right at the sunset date. A warranty that no termination or renegotiation notice has been received is also needed.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the Seller formulation.** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or ~30% of FY26 revenue, and a bare "written consent" could arrive with value-destroying conditions attached.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7; DD-003)
- **Seller:** Release "to be provided following Completion". About AUD 3.2m is outstanding and not repaid (DL item 3).
- **Buyer should want:** The facility treated as Indebtedness, deducted from the price on a debt-free basis and repaid at Completion from the funds flow. A payoff letter should be delivered before Completion. At Completion there should be a signed deed of release, PPSR discharge (financing change statements) and release of any share or asset security. Any cl 8.1 change-of-control default must be waived or neutralised before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Make discharge a Completion deliverable.** A post-Completion release leaves the Buyer owning a company with AUD 3.2m of secured debt in default on change of control.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (DD-005; funds flow)
- **Seller:** The AUD 420k Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and do not appear in the funds flow. Payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are not addressed.
- **Buyer should want:** The bonuses plus all employer on-costs treated as Transaction Costs or Indebtedness and deducted from the price. They should be paid through Company payroll with PAYG withholding at or immediately after Completion, funded by the Seller. A specific indemnity should cover any shortfall, on-costs, or claims from employees who leave.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Itemise in the funds flow and deduct from the price.** The liability sits with the Company (and so the Buyer), not the Seller, and the true cost exceeds AUD 420k once on-costs are added.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1; DD-004, DD-010)
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate". The DL confirms AUD 180k is shown as open, with no proof of payment and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer should want:** Payment of all SOW3 fees with bank evidence before Completion. A confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay delivered at Completion, as a condition precedent or deliverable. A specific indemnity covering all loss from any defect in the Company's ownership or use of SOW3 Project Materials, including third-party claims and re-development costs. That indemnity should not be subject to the general cap, thresholds, time limit or disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as inadequate.** Under cl 7.3, ownership of the IP does not transfer until every fee is paid, so the risk is losing the IP itself, not AUD 180k.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6; DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material". The DL concedes that access, scope and the need for notification are unknown, for about 1,240 records of personal information.
- **Buyer should want:** Before Completion, a completed investigation and an independent forensic report showing access and scope, plus an eligible-data-breach assessment under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme in Part IIIC of the *Privacy Act 1988* (Cth), with any notification made. A specific, uncapped (or separately capped) indemnity for regulatory penalties, OAIC proceedings, notification and remediation costs, and third-party or customer claims. A retention or escrow of an appropriate amount pending expiry of the exposure. The disclosure must not qualify the indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "not material" characterisation. Require a specific indemnity plus retention.** The Seller cannot call it immaterial while its own disclosure says the facts are unknown, and Privacy Act penalties can be significant.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008, DD-011)
- **Seller:** Three related renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k) are "ordinary-course operating costs". The DL does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Copies of the renewals and their timing.
  - Confirmation of whether they are committed, terminable without penalty, related-party or linked to the sale.
  - A warranty that they were entered on arm's-length terms in the ordinary course.
  - Pre-Completion conduct-of-business restrictions requiring Buyer consent for commitments over a threshold.
  - If they were not in the ordinary course or were split to avoid approval thresholds, treatment as Indebtedness or Transaction Costs, or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the characterisation; require information first.** Three identical "related" renewals read together look like a single AUD 330k commitment that may have been split.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation (cl 12.3 / 13, 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Seller:** All limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature unless expressly stated otherwise".
- **Buyer should want:** Separate, express regimes for each category:
  - General warranties.
  - Fundamental (title and capacity) warranties.
  - Tax warranties and tax indemnity.
  - Each specific indemnity (Ironquay, privacy, bonuses, Riverlark).
  - Fraud.
  
  Each category should have its own cap, time limit and threshold, and an express statement that general limitations do not apply to the others.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the blanket default.** It is the mechanism by which every negotiated protection collapses back into the 20% / 18-month regime.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification (DD-012)
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced" by the Company share register alone. The DL expressly notes the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer should want:** Its own verification, covering:
  - ASIC current and historical extracts reconciled to the register.
  - Share issue and transfer history, including board minutes and stamp duty where relevant.
  - Constitution and shareholders' agreement checks for pre-emption or other rights.
  - PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company.
  - Confirmation that no Riverlark security attaches to the shares.
  
  At Completion: share certificates and signed transfers, waivers of pre-emption, and a fundamental title warranty with no encumbrances, on the terms in SPA-N-004.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not rely on DD-012. Complete independent verification and keep title as an uncapped fundamental warranty.** A self-maintained register is the Seller's own record, not proof of title.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer should want:**
  - **Tax:** A full tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax, with no basket and a cap of 100% of price. A time limit aligned with ATO amendment periods plus a buffer, typically 5–7 years, with no limit for fraud or evasion.
  - **IP:** Warranties on ownership, assignment of employee and contractor IP, non-infringement and open source. These should be fundamental or near-fundamental, with a higher cap and longer period, linked to the Ironquay position.
- **Recommendation:** **Treat as OPEN; nothing has been settled.** These terms have not been negotiated, and folding them into an 18-month, 20% regime understates long-tail tax and IP risk.

---

## Priority items for the mark-up

1. **Structural points:**
   - Delete the general disclosure (N-006) and the knowledge qualifier (N-007).
   - Separate the liability categories (N-014).
   - Insert a fraud carve-out (N-005).
2. **Completion deliverables:**
   - Bluefen consent (N-008).
   - Riverlark payoff and release (N-009).
   - Ironquay assignment and payment evidence (N-011).
   - Title verification (N-015).
3. **Price and funds flow:**
   - Deduct the bonuses plus on-costs (N-010).
   - Treat Riverlark as Indebtedness (N-009).
   - Treat Sandbar per the information obtained (N-013).
4. **Specific indemnities and retention:** Privacy incident (N-012), Ironquay (N-011) and tax (N-016).
5. **Economics:**
   - Cap (N-001).
   - Thresholds (N-002).
   - Time limits (N-003, N-004).

Before the mark-up goes out, the deal team should confirm whether any of these points were genuinely agreed in prior negotiations. If they were not, the covering email should expressly reject the Seller's "[STANDARD] / cleared" characterisation.

- **Buyer should want:** Before Completion, a completed investigation and an independent forensic report showing access and scope, plus an eligible-data-breach assessment under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme in Part IIIC of the *Privacy Act 1988* (Cth), with any notification made. A specific, uncapped (or separately capped) indemnity for regulatory penalties, OAIC proceedings, notification and remediation costs, and third-party or customer claims. A retention or escrow of an appropriate amount pending expiry of the exposure. The disclosure must not qualify the indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "not material" characterisation. Require a specific indemnity plus retention.** The Seller cannot call it immaterial while its own disclosure says the facts are unknown, and Privacy Act penalties can be significant.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008, DD-011)
- **Seller:** Three related renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k) are "ordinary-course operating costs". The DL does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Copies of the renewals and their timing.
  - Confirmation of whether they are committed, terminable without penalty, related-party or linked to the sale.
  - A warranty that they were entered on arm's-length terms in the ordinary course.
  - Pre-Completion conduct-of-business restrictions requiring Buyer consent for commitments over a threshold.
  - If they were not in the ordinary course or were split to avoid approval thresholds, treatment as Indebtedness or Transaction Costs, or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the characterisation; require information first.** Three identical "related" renewals read together look like a single AUD 330k commitment that may have been split.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation (cl 12.3 / 13, 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Seller:** All limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature unless expressly stated otherwise".
- **Buyer should want:** Separate, express regimes for each category:
  - General warranties.
  - Fundamental (title and capacity) warranties.
  - Tax warranties and tax indemnity.
  - Each specific indemnity (Ironquay, privacy, bonuses, Riverlark).
  - Fraud.
  
  Each category should have its own cap, time limit and threshold, and an express statement that general limitations do not apply to the others.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the blanket default.** It is the mechanism by which every negotiated protection collapses back into the 20% / 18-month regime.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification (DD-012)
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced" by the Company share register alone. The DL expressly notes the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer should want:** Its own verification, covering:
  - ASIC current and historical extracts reconciled to the register.
  - Share issue and transfer history, including board minutes and stamp duty where relevant.
  - Constitution and shareholders' agreement checks for pre-emption or other rights.
  - PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company.
  - Confirmation that no Riverlark security attaches to the shares.
  
  At Completion: share certificates and signed transfers, waivers of pre-emption, and a fundamental title warranty with no encumbrances, on the terms in SPA-N-004.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not rely on DD-012. Complete independent verification and keep title as an uncapped fundamental warranty.** A self-maintained register is the Seller's own record, not proof of title.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer should want:**
  - **Tax:** A full tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax, with no basket and a cap of 100% of price. A time limit aligned with ATO amendment periods plus a buffer, typically 5–7 years, with no limit for fraud or evasion.
  - **IP:** Warranties on ownership, assignment of employee and contractor IP, non-infringement and open source. These should be fundamental or near-fundamental, with a higher cap and longer period, linked to the Ironquay position.
- **Recommendation:** **Treat as OPEN; nothing has been settled.** These terms have not been negotiated, and folding them into an 18-month, 20% regime understates long-tail tax and IP risk.
